shipped_rows.title_o: Children's acquisition of the number words and the counting system

blind_target.title: Children's understanding of counting
blind_target.evidence_quote: The present work focused on the GaN from Wynn's (1990Wynn's ( , 1992) ) studies with no intention to test the replicability of results coming from the other tasks (i.e., the Point-to-x task or the colour control task were not administered).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Supporting this view, Large-numbers knowers (4-to 7-knowers) were found to be more likely to resort to counting for large number words than for small ones in study 1. In addition, several children switched from a grabbing to a counting strategy around four. However, the majority of participants kept a consistent strategy all along the task and many of them still succeeded at giving large numbers with a grabbing strategy. Thus, the strategy, at least as coded here, could not be considered as what makes the difference to acquire the cardinal knowledge of large number words.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report agreement with some original observations and disagreement with others; no overall replication verdict supersedes those comparisons.

prior_decision.quote: The present work focused on the GaN from Wynn's (1990Wynn's ( , 1992) ) studies with no intention to test the replicability of results coming from the other tasks (i.e., the Point-to-x task or the colour control task were not administered).
prior_decision.reason: Omitted target. The authors explicitly frame their work as a conceptual replication of the Give-a-Number (GaN) observations from both Wynn (1990) and Wynn (1992), and in Study 1 they directly re-test Wynn's (1990) counter vs. grabber strategy predictions (line 30) as well as the all-at-once generalization assumption attributed to Wynn (1990, 1992) (line 28), finding mixed support (confirming that large-number knowers count more frequently for large than small numbers, but finding sequential acquisition of large number words and no difference between terminal-counters and terminal-grabbers in reaching large-number knowledge).

luna_triage.reason: The source says it conceptually replicates Wynn’s experiments and explicitly compares the counting-strategy finding with Wynn; its reference list identifies Wynn (1990) as a separate paper. Shipped row 365 is Wynn (1992), a distinct original, so it does not represent the 1990 target.
luna_triage.omission_quote: The aim of the present study was to provide a conceptual replication of Wynn's experiments conducted nearly 30 years ago to characterize the sequence of cardinal knowledge development.
